Subject: Clearwave DPIA template — data categories question

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is Clearwave's DPIA template (we've redacted some PHI examples). Our security team has a couple of clarifying questions before we request evidence:

- In Section 2 (Data Categories) we ask whether Redwood ever processes patient-identifiable data (PHI) in hosted mode vs. private deployments. Can you confirm which deployments may have PHI in scope and what controls differ?
- For Section 5 (Data Flow & Export), do you have a canonical data flow diagram and an index of logs/audit trails we can reference?

Our timeline is tight — ideally we close this in the next 7 business days. Let me know if a short call would help.

Appreciate it,
Sarah Huang
DPIA Coordinator
Clearwave Health

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for sending the template and the timeline. Quick answers up front:

- Hosted API (default Redwood cloud) is multi-tenant and customers should not send PHI there unless they have an agreement and specific controls in place. For PHI workloads we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated reserved pools with customer data isolation.
- We have a canonical data-flow diagram and an evidence index I can share; I'm collating the specific artifacts your template calls out (audit logs, retention policy, encryption attestations, subprocessors).

I've looped in Rishi (security/compliance) and Laura (customer success) to coordinate an evidence pack and confirm expected formats. Can you confirm the items you need first: data flow, retention windows, encryption at rest/in transit, access control list, subprocessors, and DPIA sign-off? Anything else to add?

If it helps, I can drop a short evidence index PDF into a shared Drive and we can run a 30-min sync later this week.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clearwave DPIA template — evidence indexing plan

Hi all —

Following up with the evidence plan. I pulled the current artifacts and started an index (see attached). High-level notes:

- Data categories: Redwood will not process PHI on the hosted multi-tenant service unless explicitly provisioned via a dedicated or private deployment and under a signed DPA amendment.
- Controls: encryption at rest (AES-256), TLS1.3 for in-transit, HSM-backed key management available for Private deployments, per-route/token audit logging retained for 365 days by default (configurable).
- Subprocessors: list attached (standard vendors + cloud infra). We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary (attached) and a signed subprocessor addendum.

Action items for the evidence pack:
- Olga: share the data-flow diagram and created DPIA-evidence-index.pdf
- Laura: coordinate a short call with Clearwave to confirm any PHI examples they expect us to consider in the risk analysis
- Rishi: prepare the retention/export examples and redact sample audit log entries

Sarah — would a 30-min meeting Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT work for you? I can share a Drive folder link with the artifacts once Olga drops the index.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

1) For the redacted sample logs, please include an example showing tokenized patient identifier, event timestamp, and the API route name. Redact PHI but keep field names.
2) Can you confirm whether retention beyond 365 days is considered an export under our policy (we may need to persist audit records for 7 years for compliance)? If so, note the mechanism and any pricing implications.

Thursday 10:00 PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite with a brief agenda.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Sarah
